topic: The Magic of Averages: The Central Limit Theorem (CLT)

sections.title: The Hook: Chaos to Order
lecture_lines: Individual events often seem like random chaos.
But averages reveal a hidden, perfect order.
Watch 1,000 dice rolls aggregate together.
They form a beautiful, stable bell curve.
Nature loves these consistent patterns.
animations: Create a chaotic cloud of 1,000 dots in #FF5733.
Animate dots moving to form a histogram in #FF5733.
Morph histogram into a smooth Bell Curve in #3498DB.
Flash white circle (scale 1.0) around the center peak.
Fade in text 'Order from Chaos' in #FFFFFF above curve.

sections.title: Prerequisite Refresher: The Building Blocks
lecture_lines: First, understand the population distribution.
It shows all possible individual outcomes.
Next, visualize our sampling distribution.
animations: Display population of 500 irregular bars in #F1C40F.
Display text 'Skewed Distribution' in #FFFFFF.
Animate sampler box selecting 30 bars from population.

sections.title: The Core Mechanism: The Sampling Process
lecture_lines: We take repeated samples of size 30.
Each sample mean is calculated and plotted.
The chaos transforms into a bell curve.
[Asset: SampleMeanPlot] grows with every iteration.
This is the magic of the average.
animations: Pick 30 bars, animate to calculate mean.
Plot mean as a Dot in #2ECC71.
Repeat 1,000 times to animate.
Flash 'Mean' label in #FFFFFF near.
Display text 'The magic of the average' in #FFFFFF.

sections.title: The Theorem Defined: The 'Magic' Rule
lecture_lines: Regardless of the initial population shape.
As sample size 'n' increases steadily.
The distribution of means approaches normality.
It centers perfectly at the population mean.
This is the Central Limit Theorem.
animations: Display initial skewed population in #F1C40F on left.
Display n=5 noisy distribution in #FF5733 on right.
Gradually morph distribution as n increases to 30.
Finalize graph as smooth Bell Curve in #3498DB.
Highlight formula 'Normal Distribution' in #FFFFFF.

sections.title: Real-World Application: Why It Matters
lecture_lines: This allows inferences about massive populations.
Essential for quality control in industry.
Foundational for modern scientific polling.

Animate 30 batteries moving to 'Mean' calculator.
